To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the choice of plasmonic scattering medium can have a profound impact on the performance of plasmonic devices.
Al nanoparticle arrays provide the first demonstration of broadband plasmonic photocurrent enhancement, with an efficiency enhancement of 22% in thin-film GaAS photodiodes.

the use of Al nanoparticles as scattering media in thin film solar cells can result in broadband photocurrent enhancement, due to a blue shift of their localized surface plasmons, which is not observed in Au or Ag nanoparticles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel materials and device architectures for the fabrication of efficient, broadband and stable solar energy harvesting devices.
the development and application of novel nanostructures for light management in photovoltaics and photodetection.
the design, fabrication and characterization of novel nanostructures for plasmon enhanced solar cells and photodetectors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of aluminium nanoparticles in plasmonic photovoltaics provides the best balance between far-field scattering enhancement and plasmon resonance losses, resulting in a broadband enhancement in photocurrent.
the choice of metal for plasmonic nanostructures is not only determined by the plasmon resonant frequency and scattering properties, but also by the parasitic absorption losses that can occur.

Al nanoparticle arrays are the best choice for plasmon enhanced solar cells, and that the trade-off between far field scattering and parasitic absorption is a crucial factor to be taken into consideration when designing plasmonic solar cell architectures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of Al nanoparticles in thin-film solar cells provides the first example of a broadband plasmonically enhanced solar cell.

the use of plasmonic nanostructures can provide broadband absorption enhancements in photodiodes, but only when the plasmonic resonance is sufficiently blue shifted to avoid absorption at the plasmonic band.

we have demonstrated a new approach for the design of plasmon-enhanced photodiodes, which exploits the unique properties of Al to mitigate the trade-off between far- and near-field scattering effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of scattering medium can be a critical factor in the design and optimization of plasmonic solar cell architectures.
, in order to achieve broadband plasmon-enhanced photocurrents, the plasmonic resonance needs to be shifted into the blue.
plasmonics in thin-film photovoltaics is not a panacea, but can provide significant performance improvements when carefully implemented.
